B.D. - Railway Track, under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").

Notification dated 31.10.2000, under Section 4 of the Act, qua laying of Nangal to Talwara broad gauge railway line was published and notification under Section 6 of the Act had been issued on 04.05.2001 (published in Govt. Gazette on 19.05.2001).

 2(b).
The claimants and others received the compensation amount under protest and they pressed for determination of market value of their property(ies) by the learned District Judge, Una.
In sequel, the Land Acquisition Collector, Una, referred the matter to learned District Judge, Una (learned Reference Court).

The claimants contended before the learned Reference Court that the acquired land was barani abal and its market value was not less than Rs.50,000/- per marla, so the Land Acquisition Collector had not paid compensation,
as per the market value.
The land had been acquired in parts, therefore, the value and utility of the land has decreased.
The Award of the Land Acquisition Collector is not in accordance with law and is very less.

Lastly, the claimant claimed compensation @ Rs.50,000/-
per marla.
2(c).
The Land Acquisition Collector, respondent No. 1 before the learned Reference Court (respondent No. 4 herein), by filing reply to the petition, contested the claim of the claimant.
Respondent No. 1 raised preliminary objection of estoppel.

On merits, it was averred that total compensation of Rs. 74,962/- and Rs. 27,474/- has been .
awarded to the claimants and others.
It is further averred that assessment of the acquired land was done after considering all the transactions and spot situation.
The claimants did not raise any objection at the time of announcement of the award and received the compensation without any protest.
Respondent No. 1 denied that the price of the land was Rs.50,000/- per marla.

4. The learned Reference Court after deciding issue No. 1 in favour of the claimants, issue No. 2 against the respondents, allowed the petitions, including the petition filed by the claimants, and awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 90,000/- per kanal for all categories of acquired land, as Section 19 of the Act.

r to per their respective shares recorded in the statement under The learned Reference Court, in addition to the market value of the land, held the claimants entitled for the amounts calculated at the rate of 12% per annum on the enhanced market value for the period commencing from the date of publication of the notification under Section 4 of the Act, i.e., 31.10.2000 to the date of the award of the Land Acquisition Collector, dated 13.09.2001, under Section 23(1-A) of the Act.
The claimants were also held entitled to a sum equivalent to 30% of the aforesaid market value of the land, in consideration of the compulsory nature of acquisition under Section 23(2) of the Act.

The claimants were also held entitled to interest on the compensation amount awarded by the learned Reference Court, in excess of the sum awarded by the Collector, as compensation, at the rate of 9% per annum from first year, .
that is w.e.f. 13.09.2001, i.e., the date of award and at the rate of 15% per annum for the remaining period i.e. 13.09.2002 to the date of deposit of enhanced compensation in the Court.

5. Feeling aggrieved, appellant (General Manager Northern Railway) preferred the instant appeal,
which was admitted for hearing on 16.03.2015.

6. Learned Central Government Counsel has contended that the learned Reference Court has fallen into error by enhancing the market value of the acquired land at the uniform rate of Rs.90,000/- per kanal for all categories of the acquired land.

Conversely, it is contended by the learned Senior Counsel for the claimants that since their land was acquired for the same purpose, as such the learned Reference Court has rightly awarded the compensation for the acquired land at the uniform rate, regardless of its categorization.

7. I have heard the learned Central Government Counsel for the appellant, learned Senior Counsel for respondents No. 1 to 3 (claimants), learned Additional Advocate General for respondent No. 4 and meticulously .
examined the records.

It is well settled principle of law that if entire land is acquired for the same purpose, then the claimants are entitled for compensation for the acquired land at the uniform rate, regardless of its categorization.

Reference in this regard can be made to General Manager, NHPC & another vs.
Rattan Dass & others, 2018 (2) SLC 739, relevant paras whereof, for the sake of ready reference are extracted hereunder:

sentences.text: "8. At the outset, it may be observed that it is settled principle of law that if the entire land is put for a public use and no area is left out for carrying out any developmental activity, then the claimants are entitled for compensation for the entire acquired land, at uniform rates, regardless of its categorization.

This aspect of the case has been considered by a coordinate Bench of this Court in RFA No. 282 of 2010 titled Suresh Kumar and others vs. Collector Land Acquisition, NHPC, decided on 22.10.2016 alongwith connected matters, wherein it was observed as under:
"26.

Raghubir Singh & others, (2010) 11 SCC 581

irrespective of the classification and the category of land.

Admittedly, the facts of the instant case and that of in Bhagat Ram's case (supra) are similar as in the instant case also, the land was acquired for the same purpose, i.e., laying of Nangal-Talwara Board Gauge Railway Line and the learned Reference Court has redetermined market value of the acquired land, irrespective of its nature and classification, .
therefore, the judgment (supra) is fully applicable to the facts of the instant case.

11. In view of what has been discussed hereinabove, the appeal sans merits, deserves dismissal and is accordingly dismissed.
